history.summary: Built in 1801 by Laxman Vithu and Deubai Patil, the Shree Siddhivinayak Temple on SK Bole Road, Prabhadevi (Dadar), Mumbai, enshrines a single black-stone idol of Lord Ganesha — Siddhivinayak, 'Ganesha who grants wishes'. It is among the most visited temples in India, famed for fulfilling devotees' wishes. The Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Temple Trust also runs charitable activities including medical support, a dialysis centre and educational resources. Coordinates are taken from the temple's listed address (19.016954, 72.830279) — approximate; opening hours should be confirmed against the trust's current schedule before visiting.

town_description: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial and entertainment capital, spread across seven islands on the Konkan coast along the Arabian Sea. Home to well over 12 million people, it blends colonial-era landmarks with one of the country's densest clusters of historic temples and pilgrim sites. It is connected nationally and internationally through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, two major railway zones, and an extensive suburban rail and road network.
